Tessa / Sean —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. A couple of things I promised to clarify for our internal folks so we can pick a path:

- Primary concern: predictable latency under burst traffic (surgery scheduling spikes).
- Secondary: we need guarantees around data isolation and audit logs for regulatory reviews.
- Team expects a recommendation between: hosted API with SLOs, dedicated reserved capacity, or a private VPC instance (on-prem not required yet).

Can you send a short decision aid (pros/cons + expected SLAs and typical costs) that we can share in tomorrow's architecture sync? Also, please include the minimum information your team would need from us to qualify us for Dedicated vs Private.

MedTech Insights

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@medtech-insights.com>, Priya Raman <priya.r@medtech-insights.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery

Thanks Oliver — good notes. We want to make this as actionable as possible for your architecture sync, so attached is a one-page "tenancy decision runbook" and a short spreadsheet that maps typical workload signals to our recommended deployment mode. High level:

- Hosted API: fastest to ship, predictable median latency, but higher tail variance during global spikes; best for teams prioritizing time-to-value and flexible model choices.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and tightened latency SLOs (we can commit to p50/p95 targets in the SLA for a given commit). Reduces noisy-neighbor risk and is cost-efficient at steady sustained volume.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): maximum isolation and control (KMS integrations, private control plane); needed when you require full network boundary and customer-managed infra. Higher operational lead time.

Specific to your burst/spike question: Dedicated provides the easiest path to meeting strict p95 targets because we can size and set autoscaling policies for your peak windows. Hosted can be configured with burst policies and priority routing but it's subject to multi-tenant routing fallbacks during extreme events. Private gives you the most control but requires lead time for networking and security approvals.

What we need from you to recommend Dedicated vs Private:
- Typical and peak RPS (per-minute distribution if possible)
- Target p95 latency for inference (ms) and acceptable error budget
- Data residency/KMS constraints (do any payloads need to stay in customer-managed keyspace?)
- Compliance box checks you must pass (SOC2, HIPAA evidence requests)

Next steps I suggest:
1) I'll share the short runbook + cost/maths slide with your architecture sync (attached).
2) Sean can propose a sizing sketch if you send the RPS/time-series.
3) If you want Dedicated, we'll provision a proof-of-concept pool for a 2-week soak.

Flagging Vanessa for procurement coordination and our Dedicated onboarding flow.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: tenancy-decision-runbook-v1.pdf, redwood-deploy-options-comparison.xlsx

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's discovery

Oliver — quick note from the infra side. I looked at the sample traffic you dropped in the Drive link. A couple of practical points:

- If your p95 requirement is <= 200ms at peak, Dedicated is the lowest friction route to guarantee that. We'll size the GPU pool, set autoscaling thresholds, and apply priority queuing for your key routes.
- For noisy-neighbor concerns: Dedicated eliminates co-tenant scheduling on the same GPU hosts and gives you reserved slots. Hosted uses continuous batching across tenants which improves cost but can increase variance during correlated spikes.
- For compliance: our Private VPC option supports customer KMS + configured audit-forwarding (we'll provide the SOC2 artifacts). Note that Private requires networking changes (VPC peering, firewall rules) and about 3-4 weeks of pre-provisioning depending on region.

If you can share the 7-day RPS histogram and your target p95, I can sketch a pooling recommendation and a rough committed cost estimate. I'll also include a short note on what logs/artifacts we can provide for your auditors.

Sean
Head of Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference

Tessa / Sean —

Thanks for the clear doc and quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our compliance and SRE leads:

- Target p95: 180ms (inference only), with a soft error budget of 1% monthly.
- Peak: we have predictable daily spikes (08:00–10:00 local) and a weekly higher spike on Wednesdays tied to batch uploads. Peak RPS will likely be ~6x baseline for ~15 minutes.
- Compliance: HIPAA is a yes; we also need audit-forwarding and retention of logs for 1 year. We prefer KMS customer-managed keys if possible.

We'll export the per-minute RPS for the last 30 days by EOD and share the Drive link. For now, please proceed with a Dedicated size sketch and a note on what the 2-week PoC would look like operationally (what we validate, what telemetry we'll get). Also call out fallbacks — e.g., if dedicated pool is saturated, what automatic behaviors kick in?

Priya
Senior Platform Engineer | MedTech Insights
